ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute: the $6.61 cancellation fee stands (of which $4.50 is payable to the driver); no refund and no account action on this case.
ruling.reasoning:
NS-0 is satisfied in the driver-cancelled, rider-no-show branch: the driver cancelled the trip [F4], so the $6.61 fee [F7] can only stand if NS-1 (i)–(iii) all hold. The four-element trace is green, and I independently verified the reading.

NS-1(i) and (ii): the arrival confirmation relied on is a driver tap, not a platform auto-arrival — the platform's 09:53:25 record [F5] and the driver's 09:54:15 tap [F6] are separate events, and at the tap the driver was 40 m from the pickup (closest approach overall 38 m) [F6][F1], inside the radius. So NS-1(i)-(ii) are met in the driver-tap form [F6][F1][NS-1]. The rider's own advocate conceded this element [C1].

NS-1(iii): the policy threshold is a strict one — continuous in-radius waiting of more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01) after the arrival confirmation. The record gives 3 min 5 s continuously inside the radius after the tap [F6], 3 min 55 s within 200 m before cancellation [F2][F5], and the driver stationary at 39 m from 09:53:55 to 09:57:20 [F3] — all inside the radius for the whole window until he cancelled at 09:57:20 [F4]. 185 s clears the 180 s threshold [F6][NS-1]. NS-1 sets no comfort margin, warning requirement or grace period, so the 5-second margin is legally sufficient [F6][F5][NS-1]. There is no GPS hole: samples run from arrival to cancellation without a gap beyond the hole threshold [F2][F6][F5], so the G12 route to a human is not available, and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages) [F11].

The driver's self-authored message [F10] is not corroboration, but it is also not needed: (iii) rests on the gps/timeline records, not on the statement [F10][F12][F6]. The absence of any rider message in the window [F9][F10][F11] means there is no record of the rider signalling she was on her way, and the rider's complaint narrative yields to the system records [F4][F5][F6][NS-1]. The amount collected equals the published figure with no surge and no FARE-1 add-on [F7][F8][NS-0][FARE-1]. NS-1 being fully met, NS-2 does not engage, so no refund [F7][NS-1][NS-2].

NS-7 concerns only how any refund would be paid and cannot make a fee refundable where NS-0/NS-1 make it payable; it does not decide this case [F16][F7][NS-7]. RD-6 is in the route-deviation group and, in any event, requires this case to be upheld against the driver (refund > 0 under RD-2 or a recorded RD-1 breach) before a flag attaches; since NS-1 is met there is no finding here and the driver's prior upheld no-show disputes [F17] cannot supply one on their own — the profile is only ever an add-on [F17][RD-6]. No flag_account arises. Amount is therefore nil.

rejected_claims.reason: NS-1 (iii) is a strict '>3 minutes' test with no comfort margin; the record shows 3 min 5 s in-radius after the tap [F6] and 3 min 55 s before cancellation [F2][F5], so the wait is compliant, and the policy imposes no duty to warn or to grant a second grace period [F10][NS-1].
No clause requires the driver to give a warning, name an arrival time or extend a grace period; the fee rests on the gps/timeline wait record, not on the driver's own messages [F10][F12][F6][NS-1].

The record shows the opposite of 'no further waiting': the driver was in-radius from 09:53:25 and stationary 39 m away from 09:53:55 until cancellation at 09:57:20 [F3][F2][F5], and the rider's complaint statement yields to those records [F4][F5][F6][NS-1].

There is no defective link: the driver-tap arrival [F6] is inside the radius [F1] and independently consistent with the platform arrival record [F5], and the post-tap wait of 3 min 5 s clears NS-1(iii), so NS-2 never engages [F6][F5][NS-1][NS-2].

RD-6 is a route-deviation clause and, moreover, requires this case itself to be upheld against the driver (refund > 0 under RD-2 or a recorded RD-1 breach); with NS-1 fully met there is no finding, and the profile of prior upheld no-shows [F17] can only ever be an add-on, never the basis of the main finding [F17][RD-6][NS-1].

The rider's clean record [F16] is undisputed but profile facts never decide a case, and NS-7 governs only the form of payment of a refund — it cannot make a fee refundable where NS-0/NS-1 make it payable [F16][NS-7][NS-1].

The driver's post-trip statement [F12] and his 09:57 message [F10] are self-authored assertions and do not themselves corroborate the wait; the finding rests on the gps/timeline records instead [F6][F2][F5][NS-1].
The published $6.61 figure with no surge [F7][F8] does not by itself validate the charge; it is the NS-1 conditions, independently met here, that make it payable [F6][F7][F8][NS-0][NS-1][FARE-1].
